claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 can be synthesized by arc melting.
The starting alloy is a homogenized liquid made from high-purity elements.
Adding approximately 2 at.% B to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 will improve its glass-forming ability.
Adding approximately 2 at.% B will increase the thermal stability of the alloy's amorphous state.
Phase-diagram-guided optimization of B content can avoid unwanted boride formation.
Melt spinning at cooling rates of 10^5–10^6 K/s can produce an amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 ribbon.
Phosphorus and high mixing entropy enhance the glass-forming ability of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
B atoms will segregate at incipient nucleation sites in the supercooled Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 liquid.
B has low solubility and a strong segregative tendency in this alloy.
B preferentially partitions to heterogeneities in the melt.
B partitioning disrupts the development of long-range atomic order required for crystallization.
B addition will lower the critical cooling rate required to form a fully amorphous alloy.
B addition will increase the DSC crystallization-onset temperature relative to the undoped baseline.
B addition will reduce DSC exothermic peak magnitudes relative to the undoped baseline.
Reduced DSC exothermic peak magnitudes would indicate improved thermal stability.
The beneficial effect is conditional on B remaining below the concentration at which borides or other deleterious phases form.
Excessive B or deviations from the specified processing conditions could eliminate the improvement.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as a liquid produced by arc melting, whereas the intervention says B is introduced 'into the melt prior to arc melting.' Arc melting is what produces the melt, so the stated sequence is internally inconsistent or at least operationally ambiguous.
